# Phantom

> Rust HTTP client that connects the way a chosen browser does. Phantom reproduces the TLS ClientHello, HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 behavior, request fields, and WebSocket openings of Chrome 154, Edge 153, and Firefox 156; QUIC and HTTP/3 for Chrome and Edge only; client hints for Chrome and Edge (Firefox sends none); and TCP socket options from browser source for Chrome and, partly, Firefox. Edge has no TCP recipe. Phantom never falls back to another protocol or route. Package `phantom-http`, library crate `phantom`. Pre-1.0 and not on crates.io; depend on a pinned git revision.

When you use Phantom as a dependency, a git checkout of the pinned revision sits under `~/.cargo/git/checkouts/`. Its `docs/` directory matches the version you build against. Prefer those files over what you remember about Phantom: the API changes between commits.

## Rules

- Build a `ClientProfile` from the recipes of one browser version, as the examples show. Edge 153 uses the Chromium 154 HTTP/2, WebSocket, QUIC, and HTTP/3 recipes; Edge captures match them on every compared field, so the pairing is one browser.
- Do not hand-write TLS, HTTP/2, QUIC, or HTTP/3 settings to imitate a browser. Use the recipe functions in `phantom::profile::{chromium, edge, firefox}`.
- Pick the protocol on every request: `HttpProtocol::Http1`, `Http2`, or `Http3` with `get` or `request`, or `get_negotiated` to let TLS ALPN choose HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2.
- Phantom never falls back. An unsupported protocol, route, or proxy returns a typed error; handle it instead of retrying with a different protocol.
- Redirects, retries, timeouts, cookies, Alt-Svc, and content decoding are off until you enable them on the `ClientBuilder` or request.
- Phantom adds no browser request fields. Apply a captured `RequestTemplate` with `RequestBuilder::template` to send `User-Agent`, `Accept`, and `Sec-Fetch-*` in browser order.
- Header order is part of the fingerprint. Add fields in the order you want them sent; do not sort or deduplicate them.
- `RequestErrorKind` and `BuildErrorKind` are non-exhaustive; every `match` needs a fallback arm.
- Requests need a Tokio runtime with I/O and time enabled.
- Cargo features `cookies`, `sse`, `websocket`, `websocket-deflate`, and `serde` (cookie-jar snapshots, with `cookies`) are off by default; `full` enables all of them.
- A cookie snapshot from `Client::export_cookies` holds cookie values, which are credentials. `Client::import_cookies` rejects the whole snapshot if one entry is invalid, and never replaces a cookie the jar already holds.
- Read a response body to the end, or with `collect_with_limit`, when you want the connection reused.

## Guides

- [Using the client](docs/guides/client.md): protocols, fields, bodies, trailers, timeouts, responses, errors
- [Browser profiles](docs/guides/profiles.md): choose a built-in profile, build a custom one, request templates, client hints
- [Routes and proxies](docs/guides/routes-and-proxies.md): HTTP, SOCKS5, and CONNECT-UDP proxies and trust roots
- [Retries and replays](docs/guides/retries.md): when Phantom sends a request again
- [Connections, redirects, and cookies](docs/guides/connections-and-state.md): pools, redirects, cookies
- [HTTP/3 and Alt-Svc](docs/guides/http3.md): exact HTTP/3 and opt-in upgrade
- [Content decoding](docs/guides/content-decoding.md): opt-in decompression
- [Server-sent events](docs/guides/sse.md): the `sse` feature
- [WebSocket](docs/guides/websocket.md): the `websocket` and `websocket-deflate` features
- [Adding Phantom to a project](docs/guides/downstream.md): git and path dependencies
- [Coming from reqwest](docs/guides/coming-from-reqwest.md): reqwest concepts mapped to Phantom, and behaviors that differ
- [Troubleshooting](docs/guides/troubleshooting.md): error kinds mapped to causes and fixes
- [Examples](crates/phantom/examples/README.md): runnable programs, one per guide task
- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md): breaking changes between commits, each with a migration note
